number_of_offences: Number of offences/counts charged: 5; Number of offences finally upheld: 2
premeditation_planning: The court found premeditation/planning as the replacement of the partnership deed was done with the connivance of the appellant and others
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the allegations that the partnership deed dated 5.3.2002 was replaced by a forged partnership deed dated 6.3.2003 with the connivance of the appellant and other officers in his office. The court also accepted the reports submitted by the Addi. Excise Commissioner and the Deputy Commissioner of Excise indicating the involvement of the appellant in the replacement.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the credibility of the main witnesses by noting that the partnership deed dated 6.3.2003 could not have been executed as one of the partners was present for the excise auction on 6.3.2003, contradicting the document's execution at Bhopal on the same date.
trial_duration: Offence: 2003-2004; Trial judgment: 10.4.2008; High Court: 11.11.2008; Supreme Court: Not stated
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Ashok Shrivastava, Ankur Kulkarni, Pragya Baghel, Manik Karanjawala; Counsel for the State: P.S. Patwalia, Arvind Varma, Sumeer Sodhi, Gagan Gupta, Senthil Jagadeesan, C.D. Singh, Sunny Chaudhary, Aditi Mohan, Deepika Shari, Damini Hajela
investigation_status: Complaint registered, inquiry reports submitted, case referred for further inquiry, complaint filed in court
appeal_history: Trial court: Case registered on 10.4.2008; High Court: Application dismissed on 11.11.2008; Supreme Court: Appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the complaint filed by respondent no.1 contained serious allegations of cheating by replacing the partnership deed dated 5.3.2002 with a forged deed dated 6.3.2003, and that the High Court's dismissal of the application for quashing the complaint was erroneous. They also emphasized that the complainant was aware of the developments and that the delay in filing the complaint was a valid ground for quashing.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the High Court erred in dismissing the application for quashing the complaint, as the complaint was an abuse of the process of the court. They contended that the complainant had delayed filing the complaint for five years, and that the State Authorities did not accept the inquiry reports, which were based on surmises and conjectures.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the court should not 'kill a still born child' and that appropriate prosecution should not be stifled unless there are compelling circumstances. It emphasized that the court should not dismiss a complaint at the threshold if the allegations have some substance.
precedent_relied_upon: Debendra Nath Bhattacharyya and Ors. v. The State of WB. and Anr. AIR 1972 SC 1607; Smt. Nagawwa v. Veeranna Shivalingappa Konjalgi and Ors. AIR 1976 SC 1947; Smt.
